name: Industry claims

subjectOf.text: The authors find no empirical evidence that hedge fund adviser registration under the Dodd-Frank Act negatively affects hedge fund performance, contradicting the industry's claims.
subjectOf.abstract: Contrary to the claims of the hedge fund industry, we find no empirical evidence that would suggest that hedge fund adviser registration under the Dodd-Frank Act negatively affects hedge fund performance.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: US hedge fund advisers subject to Title IV

subjectOf.text: Because there is no evidence of an inverse relationship between adviser size and per-unit compliance cost, industry concerns over the effect of Title IV compliance cost and possible barriers to entry for smaller funds and startups appear unjustified.
subjectOf.abstract: Accordingly, industry concerns over the effect of Title IV compliance cost and possible barriers to entry for smaller funds and startups seem to be unjustified.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Impact of Dodd-Frank Act Compliance Cost on the Hedge Fund Industry (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389423
scope_conditions: hedge fund advisers in the 2012 survey sample

subjectOf.text: The evidence contradicts the private fund industry's claim that private fund adviser registration under the Dodd-Frank Act negatively affects private fund performance.
subjectOf.abstract: This evidence contradicts claims of the private fund industry that private fund adviser registration under the Dodd-Frank Act negatively affects private fund performance.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2816408
